key_insight: MM-CondChain introduces the first programmatically verified benchmark that stresses deeply chained, visually grounded conditional reasoning (with branching and early termination) for multimodal LLMs, exposing failures that shallow-composition tests miss.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks test only shallow compositions or independent constraints and do not evaluate whether models can reliably verify and execute long, branching conditional workflows grounded in visual inputs (e.g., GUI-driven decision sequences).
method: Construct programmatic scenario generators that produce multi-step, visually grounded conditional chains with branching and early-exit paths.
Provide an automated verifier that checks whether model actions satisfy the compositional visual conditions and produce precise pass/fail labels.
Define an evaluation protocol and metrics that measure correctness across chain depth, branch coverage, and termination behavior.
impact: Enables rigorous, reproducible evaluation of MLLMs on real-world visual decision workflows (GUIs, agents, robotics), guiding improvements in reasoning, verification, and safety for multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing a multi-step conditional chain with branches and early termination (example: permission dialog -> color check -> click/skip).
Annotated GUI screenshot illustrating visually grounded conditions (icons/arrows pointing to features the model must verify).
Bar/line chart comparing model performance by chain depth and branch complexity to highlight degradation.
Pipeline diagram of benchmark generation → model interaction → programmatic verifier → metrics reporting.
paper_title: MM-CondChain: A Programmatically Verified Benchmark for Visually Grounded Deep Compositional Reasoning
paper_authors: Haozhan Shen, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Shuaiqi Lu, Xiaojun Tang
